text:
incident-bot: [P1] High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate (us-west-2) · Severity: Sev2 · Alert: 5xx_rate > 4% over 5m · links: metrics.redwood/v/5xx, logs.redwood/q/2240001234 · Pager: eng-oncall

Aisha: taking this as primary. I’m online and will own mitigation for the next 30m. Ping me for handoff. Initial ask: confirm customer impact and whether this is runtime or infra.

Sam: looking now — quick snapshot: 5xx are mostly 502/504 gateway from runtime layer, not LB. Error traces show consecutive model backend timeouts ~1500ms. No host flapping in infra metrics.

Marta: support — which customers are impacted? I see elevated errors on a few tenant IDs. Can we get a short blurb I can send to affected customers?

Sam: affected customers: tenant-omega, tenant-zen, and some self-serve traffic. Top customer tenant-omega is seeing request failures and retries. ETA for mitigation would help with comms.

Kevin: infra check — autoscaler metrics show desired nodes are fine. No instance terminations matching spike. However I see increased saturated GPU memory under the runtime pool during the same window. Could be model OOMs or KV cache pressure. Not ruling out runtime.

Aisha: thanks. Plan (short): 1) take canary traffic out of the pool -> roll back canary route; 2) scale down model variant to smaller config (reduce batch size); 3) manual scale runtime pool if needed; 4) support to notify customers. Assigning: Sam -> runtime triage & logs, Kevin -> infra scaling & node checks, Marta -> customer comms, Lucas -> secondary/coverage.

Lucas: I’ve got secondary. If you need to step off the pager or lunch, I’ll take over. Also can help run the rollback.

Sam: runtime triage notes — looking at model-serving logs: worker goroutines logging `KVCacheMiss` spiking and then `call_timeout` for downstream model process. Suggest immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 to 1024 for the canary and route stable traffic away from canary. Command-ish:

```bash
# quick scale down via infra CLI
redwoodctl routes set-weight --route canary-v1 --weight 0
redwoodctl models update-config --model-id mv1 --max-batch-tokens 1024
```

Sam: also enabling additional logging on the runtime side for 10m: `runtime.debug=kv,timeout` to capture more context.

Kevin: I’m scaling the runtime pool by +20% manually while we validate. If nodes fail to spin up, will fallback to migrating canary pods to stable nodes. Not seeing infra-level networking errors.

Marta: prepping customer message:

Support-Bot: Suggested template ready:

"Hello — we’re investigating increased request failures for some generation requests in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively mitigating; expected next update in 15 minutes. We recommend retrying with exponential backoff in the meantime. Contact support for specific impacts on your account."

Aisha: good. Execute plan now. Sam/Kevin run mitigation, Marta prepare comms, Lucas watch SLOs. I’ll keep the thread updated and mark status bits.

Sam: rolled back canary weight -> 0. Applied model config change (max-batch-tokens=1024) to canary and staged stable if needed. Watching logs.

Kevin: manual scale succeeded, +18% capacity. New nodes healthy, no pod crash loops.

Sam: error rate dropping from 5.6% to 1.1% over 6m after rollback & scale. Latency back to baseline for stable traffic.

Marta: sent customer blurb to tenant-omega and tenant-zen. Waiting for replies.

Aisha: incident-bot update: status transitioning -> mitigated (partial). We're keeping pager for 30 more minutes for stability.

Lucas: I’ll own the watch window. Aisha, if you need to sign off, let me know and I’ll take primary.

Aisha: I need to step into a meeting in 8 minutes. Handoff to Lucas — Lucas primary at 2240001322, I’ll be secondary/async.

Lucas: taking primary at 2240001322. Monitoring SLOs and log spikes. Sam/Kevin on-call for runtime/infra.

Support-Bot: Incident note appended to ticket #INC-2024-581 with current mitigation steps and customer outreach.

Aisha: post-mitigation actions (to be done in followup): 1) full root cause triage (runtime OOM vs model config) — owner: Sam. 2) runbook update: add explicit canary rollback play and autoscaler guardrails — owner: Kevin + eng-runtime doc owner. 3) postmortem template + timeline — owner: Aisha.

Sam: initial hypothesis logged in triage doc: `kv-cache pressure + large batch config on canary triggered downstream timeouts`. Will attach logs and flamegraphs.

Kevin: I’ll add autoscaler check for label mismatch that prevented rapid scale in a similar scenario; also add alert to warn when GPU mem > 85% for 3m.

Marta: will follow up with customers with RCA once postmortem is done.

Lucas: closing note — system stable for 12m, error rate <1% for 10m. If no regression by +30m we can close the pager and schedule postmortem.

incident-bot: Update: incident status -> monitoring. Next update due by 2240001540.

Aisha: thanks team. Logging this thread into the incident tracker and we’ll run the postmortem after stability window. Good handoff, Lucas.

Lucas: thanks — taking it from here.
